pages.says: China, Russia and the US signed a short four-point declaration in Shenzhen on UN reform, energy, the ICC and nuclear risk that leaves out Ukraine, Iran and Taiwan, and nobody is bound by it.
pages.weakest: "It settles yesterday's open question: one joint text, not three statements."

pages.says: European leaders and Zelensky met in Berlin, asked Russia for a winter pause on energy strikes and pledged €90bn in loans, but Putin had already ruled out talks.
pages.weakest: The unattributed pull quote "For as long as it takes..."

pages.says: Washington's rule requiring licences for top AI chips shipped to Singapore is now in force, with a 21 December deadline for shipments in transit, though it is expected to catch only about 100 extra applications a year.
pages.weakest: "A footnote records that an executive order now has officials write 'Super Intelligence'..."

pages.says: A good wooden dining chair comes down to its joints; Fredericia published a tough lab test for its oak chair while pricier famous chairs publish less.
pages.weakest: "Most makers print a designer's name and a wood; very few print what the chair survived."

pages.says: Anthropic sold shares at $83 to raise a record $81.3bn and closed its first day 17 per cent up, though below its opening price.
pages.weakest: "Shares outstanding come to 13,219,642,276..."

pages.says: Tencent released a large AI model that it says runs fast on a single high-end Mac, though every figure comes from Tencent.
pages.weakest: "The Q4_K_M build ... decoded at 48.13 tokens a second ...; Q3_K reached 50.34."
pages.reason: Assumes the reader knows GGUF, quantisation, GiB, tokens, parameters and llama.cpp pull requests; say what a reader would need to buy and what it would do for them.
pages.fixed: Every term glossed at first use; the build-by-build figures cut to one sentence; a new paragraph on the hardware needed (one 128GB machine, a 135GB download) and what it does.

pages.says: Pebble's US$75 voice-note ring, never charged and replaced after two or three years, got a good review, and the price is about to rise.
pages.weakest: The off-topic note on GrapheneOS and the Motorola Signature 27.

pages.says: Nomos now makes three classic watches with black dials and gold hands, and the gold versions cost about five times the steel ones for the same movement.
pages.weakest: "Those hands are a disaster."

pages.says: Percy Jackson's third season starts on Disney+ today, and its small set of early reviews is unanimously positive.
pages.weakest: The Dan Shotz quote appearing twice (fixed: the pull removed).

pages.says: A nine-country study finds parents use guilt less from 12 to 16, and teenagers guilt-tripped at 13 told parents less later, though the effect is small.
pages.reason: Beta coefficients a general reader cannot interpret; the tiny-effect box seems to contradict the body; cut the Reddit aside.
pages.fixed: Effect sizes put in plain words; the box now affirms the body's link and calls it real but small; the Reddit aside moved to the sources line.

pages.says: PSLE results come out on Tuesday, families then have a week to rank six schools, and parents should talk about feelings before the score.
pages.weakest: "Under Full Subject-Based Banding, AL5 or better in a subject opens it at G3 or G2."

pages.says: Shares fell on Anthropic's debut day and dropped below their long-run trend line, while government bonds rose and cushioned a balanced portfolio.
pages.weakest: The Lean lines, never explained.

pages.says: Japan's bond yields are near 3 per cent and the yen is still weak, because inflation eats most of that return.
pages.weakest: "The standing call is a real-rate shock... Held since No. 162"
pages.reason: The Call and the dashboard assume earlier issues and jargon; the China credit paragraph is off the yen story.
pages.fixed: The Call opens with a plain definition of a real-rate shock; dashboard trend words made plain; the China paragraph replaced by the BoJ's December meeting, with one yuan line tied to the yen.

pages.says: Wild swimming is a big and growing hobby, from Hong Kong's 4,000-swimmer harbour race to the rare Channel soloists, but in Singapore it has to be done carefully.
pages.weakest: "...is the subject of these three pages, and this one is about how people fall in and how many have."

pages.says: A swimming wetsuit's price buys flexibility more than warmth, from a £69 rental to a £999.99 flagship, plus custom suits and smart goggles.
pages.weakest: "Those are maker's claims; no independent drag test was found."

pages.says: Purist swimmers race in just a costume under strict rules, newcomers argue over changing robes, and the sport carries real risks from drowning and sewage.
pages.weakest: The £0 to £999.99 stat box repeating p17.
pages.reason: Restates p17's prices in the starter list and the stat box; use the space for something new on culture or risk.
pages.fixed: Stat replaced with the 57% inland drownings; the starter list points to p17; new ActiveSG competency and Singapore open-water race-entry rules added.

pages.says: A review of 24 trials found only hard team sport raised a blood marker of bone building, but a separate trial shows heavy lifting builds bone.
pages.weakest: "the abstract rates certainty 'moderate to low' while the figure's own panel says 'High'."

pages.says: Christmas Wonderland opens on 27 November with S$9 advance tickets, and the page lists concerts and Tokyo exhibitions worth planning around.
pages.weakest: The concert listings that each say prices are not on the promoter's page.

pages.says: BB.Q opens a food-court stall at VivoCity, a pot-rice shop opens nearby, and a chef serves a S$150 menu in his Hougang flat.
pages.weakest: "No diner has eaten at the VivoCity stall..."
pages.reason: Leads on a stall with no prices or menu, and both boxes say it is too new; lead with Pugners Dining or Sagye Lite.
pages.fixed: Relead on Pugners Dining's S$150 menu with its own Chatter and a Sceptic on the free media tasting; BB.Q cut to one paragraph and a ledger line.

pages.says: Japan's courts recognise that a voice is protected, yet Kenjiro Tsuda lost his case against an AI clone, and 'voice rights' is a phrase of the year.
pages.weakest: "his side put the average at 1.47 million views..."

pages.says: Japan's image right was built by judges from the Pink Lady case, and the ministry's guideline stretches it to the voice: famous voices get a price, ordinary ones only dignity.
pages.weakest: The paragraph on photo sizes and page numbers.

pages.says: Japan's actors' union set its own consent rules and a licensing market is growing, while it is undecided whether the person or the agency owns the voice.
pages.weakest: Okubo quoted before he is introduced (fixed).
